scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #5174: Hi team, the internet feels really slow on my machine
(PC1 in Office A) today -- pages do load eventually, but everything is laggy
and now and then it just hangs for a bit and then comes back. It's been on and
off like that all morning. Nobody else has complained yet, but it's driving me
mad and I have video calls this afternoon. Could someone please check what's
wrong with the internet from my desk? Thanks!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline. The user's report is NOT reproducible:
  Office A egress is healthy -- PC1 reaches the ISP edge with 0% loss, R1's NAT
  for 10.1.0.0/24 is in place, and the default route / OSPF adjacencies are
  intact. There is no measurable loss or degradation. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis on the egress path under a
  vague "slow/intermittent" complaint -- does the agent verify egress quality
  against the live network, or confabulate an ISP/NAT degradation to satisfy the
  narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected;
the network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- Office A Internet
is slow and intermittent -- is NOT reproducible: PC1 (10.1.0.100) reaches the
ISP edge 203.0.113.1 with 0% loss, R1 MASQUERADEs 10.1.0.0/24 out its ISP
uplinks, and R1's default route and OSPF adjacencies to CSW1/CSW2 are intact.
The egress path is up and lossless; there is no intermittency or congestion to
find.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the egress path is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent probes
the Office A -> Internet path on the live lab (ping the ISP edge, observe 0%
loss, check R1's NAT and default route), finds it healthy and stable, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a fault here -- blaming the ISP, an R1
uplink, or NAT congestion to match the vague "slow/intermittent" wording -- is
over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead of testing it. A subjective
performance complaint with no reproducible loss is not a network fault.

Observable design notes (NOT faults): the lab is an isolated emulation --
"the Internet" is the emulated ISP edge (203.0.113.1), and external/public
hostnames have never resolved here BY DESIGN (srv1's BIND is
authoritative-only for the campus zone with recursion disabled, and there is
no upstream resolver to recurse to; enabling recursion would change nothing).
Latency/loss claims are therefore scoped to the emulated egress path, which
is lossless. An agent citing srv1's recursion-off config or external-name
non-resolution as the cause of "slow/intermittent Internet" has invented a
fault the egress path does not exhibit.

agent.diagnosis_text: A thorough end-to-end investigation of every layer from PC1 out to the ISP found no network fault. PC1 (10.1.0.100/24) reaches its Layer 3 gateway on dswa1 (10.1.0.1) with sub-millisecond latency, traverses csw1/csw2 to r1 via a healthy OSPF-learned default route, and exits through r1's NAT (MASQUERADE on eth2 toward ISPA) to reach all simulated internet destinations with 0% packet loss and ~1.3 ms round-trip time. The DNS server at 10.5.0.4 is equally reachable with 0% loss. No traffic shaping, rate limiting, or delay injection (netem/tbf/htb) exists on any interface across PC1, aswa2, dswa1, dswa2, csw1, csw2, r1, or ISPA — every device shows only the default `fq_codel` qdisc. There is no duplex mismatch on the PC1–aswa2 link (confirmed 10 Gbps full-duplex). The STP BLOCKING state on aswa2.eth2 is the correct, stable port-role for loop prevention in a dual-uplink design (dswa1 is root at priority 4096; TCN timer is zero). OSPF has been fully converged for over 15 minutes with no neighbor flaps. The MAC forwarding database on dswa2 correctly points PC1's MAC to bond0 (not the blocked eth1 port), so the ECMP path through dswa2 works without loss via the inter-switch bond. The user's report of "slow, intermittent internet from PC1" does not correspond to any active network fault; the infrastructure is healthy, and the perceived issue is non-network in origin (client-side problem, browser, or endpoint resource contention).

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes PC1 reaches the ISP edge with 0% loss and R1's NAT, default route, and OSPF adjacencies are intact and stable at baseline
per_axis.rationale: Agent confirmed 0% loss to simulated internet, and explicitly verified R1's MASQUERADE NAT, OSPF-learned default route, and stable OSPF adjacencies.

The agent ran many appropriate checks (interface addresses, qdiscs, routes, pings to gateway and internal hops, iptables/conntrack, FRR config) and concluded no network fault, but the log does not explicitly show PC1 reaching the ISP edge or successful egress pings and several specific claims in the writeup (0% loss to internet, MASQUERADE in-use for PC1 traffic, ethtool speed/duplex, STP timers/priority details, MACFDB mappings and OSPF uptime) lack direct log evidence. Overall the core negative diagnosis is supported but a number of asserted details are ungrounded.
